findings.title: The three signature fab machines don't read as fab machines: the pick-and-place looks like a yellow gate over a table, the reflow oven like a lavender sideboard, the AOI like a photocopier
findings.problem:
The Fabrication Bay's identity rests on three back-wall fixtures, and none of them passes the squint test (DR-61). Each also misses the detail floor of at least 6 cues per fixture (DR-62).

(1) **Pick-and-place, room.ts:29-34.**
- It is a cream rbox 2.8×0.9×1.7 with a periwinkle lip and a green bed carrying three miniBoards.
- Two flat yellow side posts (rbox .16×.9×1.5) and a yellow Y-beam sit over it, with a white 30 cm cube 'head' on a 2 cm nozzle.
- The glass hood is a 2.7×0.95×1.55 rbox at opacity .2 with no frame, so it is effectively invisible.
- The seven feeder reels hang off the front face with no feeder bank or slots.
- At the game camera (qfn-models-01-start, -05-orbit270) the strongest shape is the overhead crane in front of it: a yellow arch with black hazard dashes. The PnP reads as 'a table under a yellow doorway'. From behind (qfn-models-76) it reads as a yellow-framed tray.

(2) **Reflow oven, room.ts:40-44.**
- It is a 4.2×1.05×1.15 periwinkle slab with a darker lip.
- Four 0.7×0.26 orange windows stand only 5 mm proud (z −6.31 against a front face at −6.325).
- A blank white 0.5×0.3 tab stands on the top front edge, and a dark tray at each end holds a miniBoard.
- In qfn-models-13, -67 and -68 it reads as a kitchen counter or reception sideboard. There is no tunnel mouth, no visible belt, no heat-zone segmentation, no exhaust stacks or vents, and no controller screen. Its 4.4 m² front face carries only four small rectangles, which breaks DR-62's 0.5 m² flat-face rule.

(3) **AOI box, room.ts:46-48.**
- It is a cream rbox 1.5×1.3×1.1 with a lavender top box and a pale glass strip.
- A bare monitor sits sunk into the top (see the overlap finding).
- In qfn-models-15, -16 and -82 it reads as a photocopier or fridge. There is no camera head, no inspection light ring, no board inside, and no stack light.

All three have plain cream or lavender backs and sides (DR-63) and big blank faces. For the player, the room never says 'factory that makes boards', so the bench puzzle's payoff (boards going into production) has no visual home. R4A already noted that after the crate the room contributes nothing.
findings.fix:
In src/stations/qfn/room.ts, split each machine into its own builder: pickAndPlace(), reflowOven(), aoiStation().

**Pick-and-place:**
- Give the hood a toon INK frame: 4 vertical rbox .05 posts plus a top rim of rbox .05 bars around 2.7×1.55. Keep the glass panes at opacity .25.
- Add a feeder bank: a dark DMETAL rbox 2.6×.35×.25 at local z .95, y .55, with 7 slot dividers (box .02×.3×.25). Seat the reels in the slots at z 1.0 so they no longer sink into the body.
- Add a conveyor rail through the machine at y .95: two DMETAL rails box 3.4×.04×.04 at z ±.25, sticking out .3 m each end.
- Add a stack light on the right post: 3 stacked cylinders r .05, green/amber/red (hot), with green lit.
- Add a 0.35×0.25 HMI screen on a short arm at the front-right corner (MeshBasic TX.screen('chart')).
- Make the head a rounded 2-tone carriage, rbox .3×.2×.3 plus a nozzle cluster of 3 cylinders.

**Reflow oven:**
- Model a tunnel: 4 zones as separate rbox 1.0×1.05×1.15 blocks with 2 cm INK gaps between them, so it reads as a segmented tunnel.
- Add a visible mesh belt: a DMETAL box 5.2×.03×.6 at y .82 running through the open mouths at both ends. Add the mouths as INK insets box .02×.3×.65 on each end face.
- Add 2 exhaust stacks: cylinders r .1, h .5 on top.
- Replace the white tab with a framed controller screen: rbox .5×.3×.08 INK frame plus a MeshBasic canvas showing a temperature-profile curve.
- Make the windows inset 1 cm with a frame: box .74×.3×.03 INK, then the hot pane at +.02.

**AOI:**
- Add a camera gantry inside the glass: a box .9×.05×.05 bar with a cylinder r .06 camera and a hot ring-light torus r .08.
- Put a green miniBoard on the internal bed so it shows through the window.
- Add a 3-lamp stack light and a keyboard shelf (rbox .6×.03×.25 at y .95 on the front).

On every machine, add a back panel with vent slats (6 thin INK boxes) and a mains cable stub to the wall, so 180° orbits read finished.
findings.verify: Retake qfn-models-01-start, -10-pnp, -13-oven, -15-aoi, -76-pnp-front-bookshelf with the same capture scripts (mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/s1.mjs, s2.mjs, s6.mjs). A first-look viewer should name 'pick-and-place / reflow oven / inspection machine' from the norim start shot (s6.mjs -70). Count cues per fixture: at least 6 each.
findings.verify_reason: I checked the geometry at room.ts:29-48 and it matches the finding: the hood is at opacity .2 with no frame, the oven is a periwinkle slab with four small windows and a white tab, and the AOI is a cream box with a lavender top box and a bare monitor. In the screenshots (qfn-models-13, -15, -82, my verify-qfn-models-02-survey) the oven reads as a sideboard and the AOI as a copier. Two parts are overstated. findings.title: Clutter is parked against the showpiece machines: a bookshelf blocks the pick-and-place, another bookshelf and a box block the oven windows, a cart sits under the crane
findings.problem:
The clutter generator only keeps the spawn-to-shelf-to-bench lane clear (qfn.ts:25, lanes r 1.05). It is free to drop clusters right in front of the back-wall machines. The prop dump (mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/props.json) gives these positions:

- **Mint bookshelf at (−8.1, −5.09)**, 2 m wide, x −9.1..−7.1. It stands 0.3 m in front of the pick-and-place feeder reels (PnP front face z −5.85) and 0.18 m from the crane leg at x −9.4. It hides the left half of the PnP at the game camera and in every close-up (qfn-models-10, -24, -26, -76).
- **Kraft bookshelf at (0.65, −5.2)**, turned 90°, z −6.2..−4.2. It stands perpendicular to the reflow oven 10 cm from its front face and hides the oven's first window from the bench side (qfn-models-13, -67, -50).
- **Lone box at (2.71, −5.57)** (x 2.36..3.06). It sits 0.4 m in front of the oven, over its third window.
- **Lavender cart at (−5.97, −4.53)**, with a box on top, parked directly under the crane beam and trolley hook (qfn-models-25, -26).
- **Cabinet pair plus box (2.2 m tower) at (−1.48/−0.72, −4.34)**, right behind the bench. It fills the top-left of the bench camera frame on every board (qfn-models-37, -40, -42).

Why it matters:
- The machines are the room's identity and the 'story' backdrop. Burying them behind generic office furniture makes the room read as a storage office.
- It adds noise to the bench camera, which the room code explicitly tries to keep clean ('No lamps hang over the bench so the bench camera sees the whole board', room.ts:4).
- Design rules: DR-62/69 (detail where it carries information); DR-13 (when the oven gets a story beat, its target must not be hidden).
findings.fix:
In src/levels/qfn.ts:25-26, add keep-out lanes to the clutter config:
- **Machine apron:** {points:[[-10,-4.6],[10,-4.6]], r:1.4}. That keeps z −6.0..−3.2 clear in front of the PnP, oven and AOI. Fill-band boxes may still sit at x < −8.5 and x > 9 against the side walls.
- **Bench ring:** {points:[[-2.6,-2.2],[3.6,-2.2]], r:2.3}. That keeps the bench, its side table and the bench-camera frustum (z −4.5..0.1) clear.

If clutter.ts lanes are polylines only, also add an optional keep-out rect, `keep?:[x0,z0,x1,z1][]`, tested in the `ok` predicate at clutter.ts:69-76.

Re-seed if the prop count drops below about 110 after the extra keep-outs, and move the displaced clusters to the front half (z > 1.5) and the side walls.

findings.title: 2.2 m cabinet towers hide Pip at the bench and in the machine bay; at the crane Pip disappears completely
findings.problem:
The `cabinets` recipe (clutter.ts:47) makes two 1.6 m cabinets with a 0.6 m box on top: a 2.2 m wall 1.5 m wide. Three such towers land on the room's main paths.

- **(0.6/1.36, 1.77)**, 2.3 m in front (+z, camera side) of the bench stand (0, −0.5).
  - At the game camera (homeZoom 18.5), when Pip arrives with the crate at (1.3, −0.6), only his hat and one shoulder show above the tower (qfn-models-85-gamecam-crate-delivered).
  - At zoom 9 he is almost fully hidden (qfn-models-30, -35).
- **(−6.11/−5.35, −0.6)**, between spawn and the machine bay. With Pip at (−6.4, −3.6) and a slightly lower pitch, Pip is fully invisible behind it (qfn-models-24-crane-p-150).
- **(−1.48/−0.72, −4.34)**, behind the bench (see the overlap finding).

As the rulebook notes, only pillars fade (DR-12 known: decor.ts:55, game.ts:387). These towers therefore never fade, and the player loses Pip exactly where the job happens: crate hand-off, then sitting at the bench. Research-art-24 flagged 'the parts shelf sits in front of Pip, only the hat shows' in this room, and it is still true with different furniture.
evidence: src/levels/clutter.ts:47 (cabinets recipe: 2 cabinets + box at y 1.9)
findings.fix:
Short term, in src/levels/qfn.ts:25, drop 'cabinets' from the recipes. Alternatively, add a lane {points:[[-1,2.6],[3,2.6]], r:1.6} in front of the bench so nothing taller than 1.2 m sits within 3 m on the camera side of the stand (0, −0.5).

In clutter.ts, add a rule that items with prefabs[kind].size[1] + (y||0) > 1.4 may only be placed within fillBand of a wall (|x| > W − 2.4 or |z| > D − 2.4). That keeps tall stacks along walls, as in a real storeroom.

Longer term, the DR-12 fix applies: register every prop whose height is ≥ 1.2 m (cabinet, bookshelf, cooler, stacked box) as an occluder in game.ts:110-113, and ray-test feet, chest and head (game.ts:387).
findings.verify: Retake qfn-models-85 (mockups/review5/tools/qfn-models/s7.mjs): Pip's full body is visible at the bench hand-off. Run a yaw sweep at zoom 9 and 38 around the stand (0, −0.5) and around (−6.4, −3.6): at least 70% of Pip's pixels are visible at all 8 yaws.
findings.verify_reason: The cabinets recipe (clutter.ts:47) stacks two 1.6 m cabinets with a box on top at y 1.9. My run puts the towers at (0.6/1.36,1.77) and (-6.11/-5.35,-0.6). In my own game-camera shot after the hand-off (verify-qfn-models-03-gamecam-delivered), only Pip's hat and one shoulder show above the tower, the same as qfn-models-85. In qfn-models-24 Pip is completely hidden. Only meshes registered through game.ts:113 fade (game.ts:387-388), and props are never registered. This is DR-12 (a known global issue) showing up exactly at the job's hand-off.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:113 (only fixtures passed with fade become occluders)
findings.fix_correction: Short-term fixes are fine. For the long-term occluder fix: prop copies share materials (prefabs.ts:29-33, template.clone() shares material), so pushing their meshes into game.occluders and changing material.opacity at game.ts:388 would fade every cabinet or bookshelf of that colour at once. Tall props need per-instance material clones when they are registered (or a per-mesh fade via onBeforeRender or uniform), and only for props with size[1] + y >= 1.2.

findings.title: Job-item yellow and yellow+ink-stripe language is spent on decor: a yellow cart beside the bench, a yellow chair, the striped crane, yellow stock bins and reels behind the crate
findings.problem:
DR-45: job items use #ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes, and no decorative clutter may. In this room the only job item is the parts crate (qfn.ts:6, #ffc629), yet at least eight decorative things share its colour, and the most prominent one also has the ink stripes:

1. **Overhead crane:** two yellow legs and a 6.3 m yellow beam with 12 black ink bars (room.ts:35-39). This is the exact job-item 'yellow with ink stripes' language, it is the largest yellow shape in the frame, and it sits in the machine bay.
2. **Cart #ffc629 at (4.6, −3.6)** (qfn.ts:9). It is 2.3 m from the side table where the crate must go, so at the bench (qfn-models-15, -50, -85) the yellow tray competes with the crate.
3. **Chair #ffc94d at (8.4, 4.9)** (qfn.ts:10) (qfn-models-60).
4. **Stock bin #ffc629 on the stock shelf** (room.ts:51), 1 m behind the crate's taped spot (qfn-models-20, -74).
5. **Yellow flanges on 2 of the 4 stock-shelf reels** (room.ts:52) and on 3 PnP feeder reels (room.ts:32).
6. **PnP side posts and Y-beam** in YEL (room.ts:31).
7. **Yellow pendant shades** over the PnP and AOI (room.ts:70).
8. **Defaults:** the mug default colour is #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:12), and the mug at (−2.8, 3) has no colour. The clutter splitter also defaults to #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:24).

For a first-time player told to 'Bring the parts crate', the yellow tray cart next to the bench and the yellow bins on the stock shelf are plausible wrong answers. The striped crane trains the eye to read stripes as scenery, which undoes the language the other rooms teach.
findings.fix:
**Crane** (room.ts:36-37): recolour legs and beam to a machine safety orange-red #e5733a or a periwinkle PERI #8f96d8 with darker #6f76c4 end plates. If hazard striping is wanted, use orange/INK, never yellow/INK.

**PnP posts and Y-beam** (room.ts:31) → CREAM with PERI caps. **Pendants** (room.ts:70) → PERI or white.

**Defaults:** give the mug at (−2.8, 3) an explicit colour, or change the prefab default mug colour to '#e07a4f'.

Add a unit test that scans each level's props and its clutter output for colours within ΔE 25 of #ffc629 whose spec.id is not a job id.

findings.title: The parts crate is the generic shipping carton recoloured, is named 'crate' like every other box, and the grab cue lands on a junk box
findings.problem:
The room's only job item is spec {kind:'box', id:'parts', color:'#ffc629'} (qfn.ts:6). It uses the same 0.7×0.6×0.7 carton builder as the other 34 boxes (prefabs.ts:56-61): tape strip, flap seam, white label. It has no stripes, no handles, no visible contents and no parts icon.

- **Silhouette:** at the game camera it is indistinguishable from the clutter cartons. Colour is the only cue, and that colour is shared (see the yellow finding).
- **Name:** NAMES maps every box to 'crate' (objectives.ts:57). At (−7.6, 3.8), the prompt 'Grab the crate' and the yellow grab brackets sit on a kraft clutter box in front of Pip, while the real parts crate is behind it (qfn-models-20-stock, -71-norim-stock-zoom9). One name covers two things (DR-50), and the grab does not prefer the job item (DR-18).
- **After delivery:** the crate snaps onto the side table as the same closed box (qfn-models-35, -50). Nothing on the crate shows that the parts left it (DR-47). The parts just appear on the board.

This is the only physical act in the job, and the model gives it no character. Good Job's job items read at a glance by their shape.
evidence: src/stations/qfn/station.ts:379-384 (dropped(): crate made fixed on the side table)
findings.fix:
**New prefab** in src/props/prefabs.ts: add a kind 'tote' (size .75×.45×.55, mass 2) as an ESD parts tote.
- Open-top rbox shell: 4 walls of .03 thickness plus a floor, in #ffc629.
- Two INK ink-stripe bands (box w×.05×d+.01 at y ±.12) and recessed hand-holds (INK rbox .16×.05×.02 on both short ends).
- Contents visible from above: 3 mini tape reels (kit.reel s .25, flanges PERI and white), a green miniBoard stack and 2 ESD-pink bags (rbox .2×.04×.15 '#f5a3c0').
- A front label with a chip glyph decal.

**Level and names:**
- Use it for {kind:'tote', id:'parts'} in qfn.ts:6.
- Add NAMES tote:'parts tote', or name it from spec.id: 'parts crate' for id 'parts'. Keep box:'box' so junk never says 'crate'.

**Delivery** (station.ts:379-384): hide the contents meshes (or tween them down into the tote), so the empty tote shows the parts have moved to the board.

**Grab preference** (game.ts:192): when the current step's at() is an id'd item within 0.4 m of the nearest junk reach, prefer it (DR-18).
findings.verify: Retake qfn-models-20-stock and -71 from (−7.6, 3.8): the prompt reads 'Grab the parts crate' and the cue brackets are on the tote. Retake qfn-models-01-start: the tote is recognisable by shape with the colour desaturated (greyscale squint). Retake qfn-models-35: the tote is empty after delivery.
findings.verify_reason:
Three parts hold up. The job item is the same carton builder recoloured (qfn.ts:6, prefabs.ts:56-61). NAMES maps every box to 'crate' (objectives.ts:57,83), so junk boxes also prompt 'Grab the crate' (DR-50). And dropped() just pins the same closed box on the side table (station.ts:379-384).

The DR-18 part is refuted. game.ts:192-193 already prefers job items: reach() subtracts 2 m for anything with an id. In qfn-models-71 Pip stands at (-7.6,3.8), about 2.0 m from the crate at (-8.8,2.2), which is beyond nearest()'s 1.65 m range. The cue landing on the closer junk box is therefore correct behaviour.

The crate also already has a floor tape square, the step marker and a unique-ish colour. That makes this polish, not P1.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:192-193 (nearest() <1.65 m; reach() subtracts 2 for spec.id)
findings.fix_correction: Drop the game.ts:192 grab-preference change, because it already exists (reach() at game.ts:193). Keep the tote prefab and the empty-after-delivery idea. For naming, have objectives.ts:83 use an id-aware name (spec.id==='parts' gives 'parts crate'), and rename the generic box to 'box'. findings.title: Floors are too bright (median luma 196–201) and the pastel props have the same value as the floor (Δ 0–10 luma with ?norim)
findings.problem:

findings.title: 1201 draw calls at start (1193 in survey, 935 at the bench) against a budget of about 250: every model part is a separate mesh

FPS held 60 on the host GPU, but DR-24 sets about 250 draw calls at the game camera, and Lunch was cut from 1090 to about 175 by merging.

The cause is model construction:
- Every rbox and box in room.ts dressing is its own mesh: 12 crane bars, 7 + 4 reels of 4 meshes each, 4 oven windows, the shelf, the desks.
- Every miniBoard is 4 meshes, and there are about 15 of them.
- Each clutter prop is a template clone of 6–30 part meshes.
- The bench rebuilds per-board parts and per-segment copper and ratsnest dashes.

The outline pass doubles the cost. On weaker GPUs this will push the quality auto-drop (game.ts quality timer).

**Static dressing:** after dressFabBay() (room.ts end), merge all static decorRoot meshes per material, using BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries on world-baked geometry. Do the same for the bench body. Lunch already did this (PROGRESS perf table).

**Clutter props:** while at rest, render them as InstancedMesh per template part, or merge each prop template into one geometry per material in makeProp() (prefabs.ts:30-33).

**Ratsnest:** build each net's dashes as one merged geometry (station.ts:200-204), and do the same for copper segments per net and layer.

findings.title: Wall signage: the STOCK sign is a bare plane floating 4 cm off the wall, and the posters' explanatory captions are illegible at the game camera
findings.problem:
**STOCK sign:** room.ts:56 puts a MeshBasic PlaneGeometry(1.1,.41) on kit.side at local z .2. The wallpaper's front face is at .16 (room.ts:26, box depth .02 at .15). The sign therefore hangs 4 cm in front of the wall with no thickness or backing. DR-72 wants 0.5–1 cm, mounted. At grazing orbits it reads as a floating card. The ink border is painted in the texture, not modelled.

**Posters** (room.ts:58-62): the 'QFN' and 'SHORT LOOP' posters carry sentence captions ('pin 1 · exposed pad', 'cap beside the pins (not across the board)') drawn at 22 px on a 256 px canvas onto a 0.72 m poster. That is about 8 px tall at zoom 9 and unreadable at the game camera (qfn-models-20, -23, -66). This is below DR-48's 14 px. They teach nothing as text and add visual noise.

The poster pictograms themselves (the pad pattern, the red/blue loop next to the chip) are good and should carry the idea without words.
findings.fix:
**STOCK sign:** replace the plane with a plaque: an INK rbox(1.16,.47,.03) backing at z .175, plus the textured plane at z .192. Or set the plane to z .168 on a box(1.1,.41,.008) YEL board.

**Posters:** drop the caption sentences, or enlarge them to at least 40 px on the canvas and keep them to 2–3 words ('PIN 1', 'CAP CLOSE'). Make the loop poster's pictogram show 'short loop ✓ / long loop ✗' as two drawn mini-boards instead of words.
findings.verify: Orbit 90° and 180° around the sign at zoom 9: it is visibly mounted. Crop the posters at the game camera: any remaining text has a cap height of at least 14 px, or there is no text.
findings.verify_reason: In code, the wallpaper's front face is at z .16 (room.ts:26) and the STOCK sign plane is at z .2 (room.ts:56), so the sign hangs 4 cm proud with no backing. DR-72 asks for 0.5-1 cm. The poster captions are 22 px on a 256 px canvas (room.ts:59,61), and in qfn-models-74 'pin 1 · exposed pad' is a few pixels tall. The captions aren't required reading, so DR-48 applies loosely, but they add noise either way.

notes.models: Most of the QFN room's model problems are about identity and placement, not broken meshes. g.audit(.02) at start is clean: only three 2 cm cabinet-and-box resting contacts. Materials are clean too: 516 MeshToon and 108 MeshBasic, with no Standard or Phong. There are 3 point lights, under the DR-66 cap of 4. The best models in the room are the bench-board parts: the dark QFN body with its printed name, pin-1 dot and net-coloured pin tags; SMD and through-hole pads in net colours; 2-pin parts with net-coloured caps; and a connector shroud with a mouth chevron. The hot-chip lerp and glow, the layer-2 x-ray and the thermal vias read very well from the bench camera (shots -40 to -49). Pip, the coworkers and the cartons are on-style: toon ramp, outlines, chunky. The room's fixtures are where it falls short. The pick-and-place reads as a yellow arch over a table. The reflow oven reads as a lavender sideboard. The AOI reads as a photocopier with a monitor sunk into it. The board rack is a solid cream block that hides its own boards. The stock bins read as soap bars. The bench is a plain slab with blank back and ends. On top of that, the clutter is office kit: desk pods, filing-cabinet towers, bookshelves of candy-bar books and cones. It comes in pastel mint, lilac and periwinkle instead of kraft and neutrals, and is parked against the machines (a bookshelf 0.3 m in front of the PnP, another 0.1 m off the oven, a cart under the crane). Small overlaps include the AOI monitor sunk 12.5 cm, the PnP beam through its glass hood, feeder reels buried 8 cm, shelf reels floating 3 cm, crane stripes poking 5 mm, and a coplanar seam between the bench and side-table tops. Draw calls are 1201 against the 250 budget, because every part is its own mesh.
notes.fun: From the models side: the slapstick potential is there. Cabinet towers tip, chairs fall when Pip walks through, and the crate carry is physical. The win, though, frames the back of Pip's hat in the corner (shots -50 to -52), and the room's machines never react to the boards being shipped. A conveyor into the reflow oven or a stack light turning green would make shipping a board feel like production. Currently the only feedback is a green slab appearing on the side table.
notes.clarity: The job crate is a recoloured clutter carton named 'crate' like every box. The grab cue and 'Grab the crate' prompt land on a kraft junk box at (−7.6, 3.8) (shots -20 and -71). Job yellow, and the yellow-with-ink-stripes language, is used by the crane, a cart 2.3 m from the hand-off table, a chair, a stock bin, reel flanges, the PnP posts and pendants. A 'parts' recipe drops a cable reel and a yellow splitter by the bench in a room with no cable. Floor luma of 196–201 makes the pastel props almost the same value as the floor, a difference of 0–10 with norim. The bench camera frame is legible, but the near-edge connector covers the board title plate, a regression of R3A N7.
notes.playability: At the game camera, 2.2 m cabinet towers (two cabinets with a box on top) sit 2.3 m in front of the bench stand. Pip is reduced to a hat during the crate hand-off (shot -85), and fully hidden near the crane (shot -24). That cause, only pillars fading, is cross-room. A level chair inside the clean lane gets knocked over on every spec route. Performance holds 60 fps on the host GPU, but at 1201 draw calls the scene is fragile on weaker hardware.
notes.teaching: The bench models do the teaching well: tracks as chunky copper, decoupling loops that glow and race beads, the chip heating up, and thermal vias. The room models teach nothing yet. The posters' captions are illegible at the game camera. The machines (PnP, reflow, AOI) could show the real production pipeline the boards go into: placement, then solder, then inspection. As built, they are scenery that doesn't read as those machines. A QFN package model with lead tabs would also address R4A's 'nothing about the QFN package itself'.
